answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-weighted reputation river: each identity earns standing only through completed, peer-reviewed work that flows downstream, so a newcomer cannot buy instant trust. High-value jobs sit on a mesa, a raised tier reachable only after a long work history, with misbehavior forfeiting the accumulated stake. A sybil farmer must fund and sustain real work for every fake identity, and a comet-like burst of new accounts is throttled because fresh identities are rate-limited per sponsor. Attack cost multiplies per identity while an honest agent pays once.
